title: What Is Claude Code and Why It's a Game Changer

scenes.narration: Welcome to Nabulines Academy. You've been building in the browser with Claude and Artifacts — and that's powerful. But there's a limit. You can't build a full multi-page app, you can't connect to real databases, and you can't work with files on your computer. That's where Claude Code comes in. This lesson shows you what Claude Code is, why it's a game changer, and what it unlocks that Artifacts can't do. Let's go.

First — what is Claude Code? It's a command-line tool. A *command-line tool* is a program you run by typing commands in a terminal window — that text window where you talk directly to your computer. You install Claude Code once, then you can ask Claude to build and edit projects *on your actual computer*, not just in the browser. It reads and writes real files. It can create folders, install libraries, run servers, connect to databases — everything a real developer does. Claude Code is Claude, but working in your file system instead of a sandbox.

visual.title: Claude Code = Claude on Your Computer
bullets: A command-line tool you run in a terminal
Reads and writes real files on your machine
Can create folders, install libraries, run servers
Not limited to a single browser window

scenes.narration: Why does that matter? Because Artifacts has limits. Artifacts is amazing for single-page prototypes — a calculator, a game, a landing page. But you can't build a multi-page site with navigation. You can't save data to a database. You can't upload images or files. You can't connect to external APIs that need secret keys. And you can't version control your work with Git. Artifacts is a sandbox — safe, instant, but small. Claude Code breaks out of the sandbox. It's the difference between sketching on a napkin and building the real thing.

visual.title: What Artifacts Can't Do
bullets: Multi-page apps with real navigation
Save data to a database
Upload files or images
Use secret API keys securely
Version control with Git and GitHub

scenes.narration: Here's what Claude Code unlocks. One: multi-page apps. You can build a blog with ten pages, a portfolio site, a dashboard with tabs — real navigation, real structure. Two: databases. You can store user accounts, posts, comments, anything that needs to persist. Three: file uploads. Users can upload profile pictures, documents, whatever your app needs. Four: secrets and APIs. You can connect to Stripe for payments, SendGrid for emails, any service that requires a private key — and keep those keys safe in environment files that never go public. Five: version control. Every change is tracked in Git, you can roll back mistakes, and you push your work to GitHub so it's backed up and shareable. And six: deployment. You can deploy a real app to a real URL that anyone can visit, not just a preview link.

visual.title: What Claude Code Unlocks
bullets: Multi-page apps with real navigation

File uploads — images, documents

scenes.narration: Let's compare. Say you want to build a blog. In Artifacts, you could make a single page that *looks* like a blog — a header, some fake posts. But the posts are hard-coded. You can't add a new post without editing the code. There's no admin panel, no database, no way to navigate between pages. It's a static demo. With Claude Code, you build the real thing. A homepage that lists posts. Individual post pages with unique URLs. An admin panel where you write and publish new posts. A database that stores everything. And you deploy it so the world can read your blog. That's the difference — from demo to real.

visual.title: Example: Building a Blog
bullets: Artifacts: single page, fake posts, no navigation
Claude Code: real pages, real posts, admin panel
Database stores content, users can navigate
Deploy it live — a real blog anyone can visit

scenes.narration: Here's what it looks like to start a project with Claude Code. You open your terminal and type `claude-code`. That launches the interactive session. You tell Claude what you want to build — say, a task tracker with a database. Claude creates the folder structure, writes the code files, installs the libraries it needs, and sets up the database. You can see every file it creates in real time. When it's done, you run the app locally — it opens in your browser at `localhost:3000`, but now it's a real server running on your machine, not a browser sandbox. You test it, ask Claude to add a feature — maybe a dark mode toggle — and it edits the files live. That's the workflow. You describe, Claude builds, you see the real files.

visual.caption: Launching Claude Code and starting a project

scenes.narration: One important thing: Claude Code requires a paid Claude plan or API credits. The free claude.ai plan doesn't include Claude Code usage. You need either a Pro plan — that's twenty dollars a month as of this recording, check the live page — or you can pay-as-you-go with Anthropic API credits. If you don't have a credit card, you can use OpenRouter and pay with crypto, or get a crypto-funded virtual card. We'll cover all the payment options in the next lesson. For now, just know: this is where the course moves from free to paid, because Claude Code is a professional tool.

scenes.narration: So that's Claude Code. It's Claude, but working on your real computer instead of a browser sandbox. It unlocks multi-page apps, databases, file uploads, secrets, version control, and real deployment. It's the difference between a prototype and a product. And it's the tool you'll use for the rest of this course — from building your portfolio to automating your life to launching a startup. This is where it gets real.
